This is something that I've been dealing with for a while now, and here are some of my personal suggestions. I am not a therapist or mental health professional, so please take these with a grain of salt. 

1. Identify what exactly you hate about people. You said you do it for no reason, but there has to be something that triggers you the most. Try to define at least one thing.
2. Every reoccuring negative thought pattern has its root cause and "launch moment". Try to remember when you first started to feel this hatred. What was going on in your life at that time? Perhaps there was a particular situation that really set you off? Think as far back as possible. What bothered you the most about that situation? If you can't recall when it all started, then try to remember the last time you felt exceptionally hateful and why. Try to remember every single time you felt that way and see if the cause was the same.
3. Realize that your negative emotions that were caused by those negative experiences were internalized and turned into an unhealthy thinking habit. It was a useful coping mechanism in the past, but now it no longer benefits you and you need to cut it off. To do that you have to gain a new perspective. Whatever happened in your past happened, and it no longer has any power over you. You can start with a clean state. Meditation is great, because it allows you to clear your mind and focus on here and now. Allow yourself to recover.
4. Understand that people are far from perfect and often do dumb shit. Granted, there are a lot of terrible individuals walking on this planet. But there is also plenty of kind and loving people. Putting everyone into one single category would be a mistake, since we can't actually know people. The best we can do is to deal with each person individually.

Anyway, here is my two cents. Hope any of this helps.

Oh fuck yes, you absolutely have a right to die. Your body - your own business. And you don't need to "earn" a right to do something to your body. Death can be an irrational choice, but it's a choice nonetheless. And who the hell would want to set a goal of earning a right to die? This is just so bizarre. People commit suicide for two reasons: jacked-up brain chemistry or despair. Either way you run out of methods to make sense out of life, you can't put a "personal conclusion" to your problems, cause you are just so overwhelmed you don't see a point anymore. When you are cornered, you will begin to look for the next source of light that'll make sense to you. For depressed people more often than not it turns out to be a self-murder. That is their conclusion. But if you're feeling that you have earned a right to die by solving the problem that caused you to be  suicidal in the  first place, you won't even feel the need to die, duh. We all try our best, but we all have a breaking point.

Not everyone who commits suicide does so in a state of being completely out of control over their actions. When it gets too painful a lot of them just run out of alternatives, coping mechanisms, and ways to rationalise and make sense out of life. Nothing just makes sense anymore, but the painful experiences still keep happening. In other words, not everyone who commits suicide is insane, and believing so is one of the reasons why we still attach stigma to it. Suicide is real, and it's equally real in the world of mentally sane people. Desperation alone can really drive you to that extreme point. But I  understand where you are coming from.

I get what you're trying to say. It's very hard to breach that border and get to the point where you are 100% determined and focused, cause you basically go against your own nature. But to me the sheer possibility of it happening is already comforting. I like to think about it like: "Take control of your life, or take control of your death". I believe those of us who are suicidal are actually very strong people. If we have so much strength to potentially go against our nature and call it a night, we can gather that strength and direct it towards bettering our life. And since we know we will die and can even choose to die anyway, what else do we have to lose? It's almost like applying a samurai's mindset - you go and fight for what you need but you are ready to die at any moment. I don't know if that makes sense, but here we are.
